title: Release group review from pair-check history
software_contract: review_releases(request) validates every version/check/request before processing and raises ValueError for invalid input (message unspecified), without mutation. Pair checks are undirected; the last input record for a pair supersedes earlier records, including reversed pairs. Unknown pairs are unverified, not passed. A proposed group must contain only active versions from that request's members, with every pair's latest check passed. Requests are independent, never consume versions, and follow input order. Output contains version_count, check_count, pair_count (distinct checked pairs including inactive versions), superseded_check_count (check_count-pair_count), and requests. Each request report contains request_id, eligible (active requested versions in global version input order), current, preview, proposed and changes. A description contains selected IDs in global version order, size, inactive IDs, missing_pairs (global pair order, each left/right/reason=failed or unverified), and eligible_and_compatible (no inactive or missing pair). Current may be inactive or incompatible and is reported honestly. Preview always starts empty and scans eligible versions in order, accepting a version exactly when it is compatible with every already accepted one; preview must retain this behavior even if a larger group exists. For mode=inspect, proposed and changes are null. For mode=select, proposed has the greatest possible size among eligible pair-compatible groups; ties choose the smallest integer sum(2**i) over selected positions in eligible. Empty eligible produces empty proposal. changes.add/remove are differences from current in global version order, not an objective. Singleton groups need no pair checks. No triple-level compatibility, minimum-change preference, or approximate size is permitted. CLI reads one JSON request and prints one JSON report; invalid inputs exit nonzero with no successful report.
input_domain: Object with exactly versions, checks, requests, all finite lists. Version records have exactly version_id (unique nonempty string), active (bool). Check records have exactly left, right (distinct known version ID strings), passed (bool). Repeated/reversed checks are permitted, order authoritative. Request records have exactly request_id (unique nonempty string), members (distinct known version IDs), current (distinct IDs drawn from members), mode (inspect or select). Member/current order need not follow catalogue order. No artificial version/count cap. Compatibility is explicitly pairwise according to supplied check records; these records are not executed tests or a claim about real software compatibility.
execution_assumptions: Versions represent independently selectable artifacts, not necessarily alternatives of one package. Pair-check history is supplied by the caller; no network or package installation occurs.
All reports and previews are observable. No measured workload distribution, hardware budget, encoding cost or practical benefit is supplied.
